bib.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for a Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Appendix B code listings skimmed, not line-read.

question: Can encoding human Standardized Operating Procedures into role-specialised LLM agents with structured document handoffs reduce cascading hallucination and improve multi-agent code generation?
hypothesis: SOP-style roles, structured communication and executable feedback yield more coherent software than chat-based multi-agent systems.
contributions: A meta-programming multi-agent framework with role definition and message sharing.
SOPs throughout the design, plus an executable feedback mechanism (5.4% absolute improvement on MBPP).

method.summary: Five roles (Product Manager, Architect, Project Manager, Engineer, QA Engineer) run a sequential SOP, publish structured documents to a shared message pool and subscribe to what they need. The Engineer runs unit tests and debugs for up to 3 retries. Evaluated with GPT-4 on HumanEval, MBPP and a 70-task SoftwareDev set.

limits: Cannot handle UI/front-end or multimodal scenarios; real-world requirements remain hard (Appx D.1).
Users cannot easily interrupt agents or set checkpoints.
Each project runs independently; self-improvement only modifies role constraints (Appx A.1).
SoftwareDev is the authors' own benchmark with human-scored executability and unstated rater count; main comparison uses 7 of 70 tasks.
No temperature, decoding or seed settings given; the 67% GPT-4 baseline is quoted from OpenAI, while the authors' own reruns reach 72.4-81.2%.
